newsitem.title: FRANCE: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - GAN suitors, UNISON disunity.
newsitem.headline: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - GAN suitors, UNISON disunity.

text.p: THE PROTEUS COLUMN
A race for the ownership of French insurer GAN looks like it is in the making following the decision by the French government to inject 20 billion francs to write off the group's property losses.
The main contenders are likely to be AGF and Allianz, and the reason they are both interested is the merger of Axa and UAP.

Shares in AGF soared yesterday after comments by chief executive Antoine Jeancourt-Galignani that GAN's activities would complement his own. He is looking at the new, improved Axa-UAP as a very powerful competitor and also as a group whose sheer size changes the shape of the French market. The merger of Axa and UAP created a heavyweight force which tilts the previously relatively even playing field.
So, not only does he need to achieve critical mass to compete against a bigger rival, he also wants AGF to be big enough to act as a counterweight and balance the domestic market.

As Proteus has suggested before, Allianz also sees Axa as a major rival. And, as Allianz needs to expand in important markets anyway, where better than on the front doorstep of a major competitor coming to terms with a merger? France has never been a great success for Allianz, nor indeed for any other non-French insurer. But the market is changing shape because of privatisation, and Allianz has clearly decided not to write-off its previous investment.

Other potential contenders are hard to spot. Commercial Union is a distant possibility, and General Accident could consider recreating the old French-Scottish alliance by building on its existing limited involvement in France. UK insurers have never really looked to France as a major market, but with the possibility of cross-European insurance becoming a reality, the idea of owning GAN may be attractive.
--oo0oo--

Jauch & Huebener is less than happy at the situation it finds itself in this week as a result of the Marsh & McLennan merger with its UNISON partner Johnson & Higgins. The German broker cancelled a customer meeting with UNISON bosses next week because the future of the alliance now looks shaky. Marsh is saying it would like to maintain close relations with some UNISON members, but as it already has a major presence in Germany, Jauch & Huebener may not be one of them.
Therefore it finds itself potentially without a partner and without a means of servicing global clients.
